records.title: UpdateEngine payload hash and size mismatches identify package-transfer failure
records.summary: Android update-engine codes 10 and 11 distinguish a whole-payload hash mismatch from a payload-size mismatch. Both invalidate the received package before it can be trusted as recovery input.
symptoms: OTA download completes but apply fails
ADB sideload fails during payload verification
same package fails before post-install
diagnostic_steps: Preserve the full update-engine/recovery log and distinguish code 10 from code 11 rather than relying on a generic status 1 wrapper.
Compare the local file byte count and SHA-256 with the official publisher's exact device/build artifact.
Reacquire the payload through a stable path; repeated mismatches from the same source indicate a bad artifact or delivery path.
fix_steps: Discard a payload whose size or digest does not match the trusted manifest and download the exact official artifact again.
Do not bypass hash or size verification.
prerequisites: Exact device/build target, trusted publisher URL, expected file size or digest, and enough local storage for a complete download.
expected_outcomes: A complete byte-identical payload passes whole-payload size and hash checks.
compatibility: Android A/B OTA clients exposing AOSP update-engine result codes.
known_incompatibility: These codes do not by themselves prove a bad partition or authorize a different model's package.
recovery_routes: Official full OTA or vendor recovery after exact identity verification.

scope.scope_note: Platform error semantics; device and build still determine the only compatible recovery package.

records.title: UpdateEngine signature or public-key verification failure is a trust failure
records.summary: Codes 12 and 18 mean update-engine could not validate payload signatures or create/complete public-key verification. The safe response is to reject the payload, not disable verification.
symptoms: OTA package downloads but signature verification fails
sideload rejects signed payload
payload public key verification fails
diagnostic_steps: Capture the exact error code, payload filename, source URL, expected signing channel, and device build fingerprint.
Verify that the package is an official artifact for the exact device/channel and has not been modified.
Separate payload-signature failure from AVB boot-chain failure; they occur at different verification stages.
fix_steps: Replace the rejected payload with an intact artifact signed for the target update channel.
Do not suppress signature checks or substitute test keys on a production recovery path.
prerequisites: Trusted source and exact target/channel identity.
expected_outcomes: A valid payload passes metadata and payload signature verification.
known_incompatibility: An artifact signed by another OEM, device family, custom-ROM key, or release channel remains incompatible even if its contents look similar.
recovery_routes: Official vendor OTA, full image, or supported recovery service.

scope.scope_note: Platform trust failure; never convert it into advice to bypass verification.

records.title: UpdateEngine code 51 rejects an OTA downgrade by build timestamp
records.summary: PAYLOAD_TIMESTAMP_ERROR means the update payload's maximum timestamp is older than the installed build state, so the OTA path refuses the downgrade.
symptoms: stable OTA sideload says package is older
beta unenrollment package aborts
downgrade not allowed
error_codes: Update package is older than the current build
diagnostic_steps: Record current fingerprint/build timestamp and the OTA pre/post build identifiers and timestamp.
Confirm whether the device is on a beta or newer security train than the proposed stable package.
Do not confuse recovery status 1 with the underlying timestamp rejection line.
fix_steps: Wait for or obtain an official package newer than the installed timestamp, or use the OEM's explicitly documented downgrade path with its stated data-loss rules.
Do not edit OTA metadata or bypass timestamp enforcement.
prerequisites: Exact current and target build identities and an OEM-supported transition route.
expected_outcomes: A permitted newer payload proceeds past timestamp validation.
compatibility: A/B OTA packages using update-engine timestamp enforcement.
known_incompatibility: A lower Android number is not the only downgrade signal; build timestamp and rollback metadata can block installation.
recovery_routes: Official newer full OTA or documented data-erasing return-to-stable flow.

scope.scope_note: Platform downgrade rule; OEM policy and exact builds determine the available recovery route.

records.title: UpdateEngine code 60 requires freeing space before retry
records.summary: NOT_ENOUGH_SPACE is an explicit allocation failure. The platform API says the user should be prompted to free space and retry rather than repeatedly applying the same payload unchanged.
symptoms: system update cannot allocate space
OTA preparation fails before reboot
Virtual A/B update reports insufficient space
diagnostic_steps: Record free userdata space, snapshot/update state, payload size, and whether a previous update is pending cleanup.
Confirm the exact code 60 rather than inferring low space from a generic update failure.
fix_steps: Back up and remove dispensable user files or apps, complete any vendor-supported update cleanup, then retry the same verified update.
Do not erase partitions manually to manufacture free space.
prerequisites: A recoverable Android session or OEM-supported storage-management route.
expected_outcomes: Space allocation succeeds and update preparation continues.
known_incompatibility: Freeing host-computer disk space does not resolve insufficient space reported on the device.
recovery_routes: OEM support if code 60 persists after safe storage cleanup.

scope.scope_note: Platform storage-allocation fix; no partition resize or erase authority.

records.title: UpdateEngine code 61 blocks further updates because device update state is corrupted
records.summary: DEVICE_CORRUPTED is not a network retry signal. Android documents it as a state where no further update may be applied, requiring recovery or service rather than repeated payload attempts.
symptoms: all subsequent OTA attempts are refused
snapshot cleanup fails
update state remains corrupted after reboot
diagnostic_steps: Preserve update-engine, snapshot, boot-control, and recovery logs before any reset.
Record current slot, successful/bootable flags, merge state, exact build, and whether an interrupted Virtual A/B update preceded the error.
Stop automatic update retries so the original evidence is not buried.
fix_steps: Use the exact OEM recovery path or authorized repair; do not claim that re-downloading alone repairs code 61.
prerequisites: Exact build and slot/snapshot evidence, plus a backup or explicit data-loss assessment.
expected_outcomes: A full supported recovery reconstructs a valid update state, or service identifies storage/board failure.
known_incompatibility: This error cannot safely be reduced to bad Wi-Fi, insufficient host storage, or an ordinary app crash.
recovery_routes: OEM full recovery, service tool, or authorized hardware diagnosis.

scope.scope_note: Platform terminal update-state signal; exact OEM recovery is required.

records.title: UpdateEngine code 7 means an install target could not be opened
records.summary: kInstallDeviceOpenError identifies failure opening an installation target. A recovery status 1 line is only a wrapper and cannot distinguish target access from package, cable, or downgrade faults.
symptoms: ADB sideload reaches installation then aborts
recovery reports status 1 after ErrorCode 7
OTA fails at a repeatable percentage
diagnostic_steps: Read Recovery logs and retain the underlying ErrorCode line, target partition/device path, current slot, and build.
Verify that the target partition inventory exists and is accessible in the current recovery/update mode.
Do not assume the common host progress percentage equals the actual on-device apply percentage.
fix_steps: Correct the exact target-access or state problem identified in logs, or use the OEM's supported full recovery route.
Treat factory reset only as a separately approved destructive experiment when official guidance or exact community evidence supports it.
prerequisites: Full recovery/update-engine log, exact build, partition inventory, and data-loss assessment.
expected_outcomes: The target device opens and payload application continues.
compatibility: Android update-engine/recovery cases explicitly reporting code 7.
known_incompatibility: Status 1 alone is insufficient; it wraps many different causes.
recovery_routes: OEM full OTA, software repair, or authorized service after diagnosis.

scope.scope_note: Platform error meaning only; the failed target and compatible remedy come from exact logs and Device DNA.

records.title: UpdateEngine operation hash mismatch identifies a corrupt payload data extent
records.summary: Code 29 is emitted when the calculated hash of one payload operation's data differs from its manifest hash, distinct from whole-payload hash mismatch and source-partition mismatch.
symptoms: OTA fails on a specific payload operation
retry fails at the same data offset
operation hash verification reports expected and calculated values
diagnostic_steps: Capture the operation number, data offset, expected hash, calculated hash, source URL, and whether the download was resumed.
Re-download the exact payload and compare its whole-file digest before retry.
If multiple independent downloads differ, treat the delivery source or storage path as suspect.
fix_steps: Replace the corrupted payload bytes with a verified complete official artifact; do not bypass per-operation verification.
prerequisites: Trusted manifest/artifact source and enough storage for a clean download.
expected_outcomes: Each operation extent hashes to the value declared in the signed payload manifest.
compatibility: A/B payloads processed by AOSP update-engine.
known_incompatibility: Code 29 does not prove that the installed source partition is modified; source validation has separate evidence.
recovery_routes: Retry with a verified full payload or official OEM updater.

scope.scope_note: Platform payload-data diagnosis independent of OEM brand.

records.title: Incremental OTA source hash mismatch calls for an exact full OTA
records.summary: An incremental payload applies binary deltas against specific source-partition bytes. Root, remount, partial flashing, or a different source build can invalidate those hashes; AOSP recommends clients try a full OTA after a partial OTA fails.
symptoms: incremental OTA fails on modified system
delta update says source partition hash differs
full OTA remains available
diagnostic_steps: Record current slot fingerprint and hashes for every source partition named in the failure.
Compare the installed source build with the incremental OTA's pre-build and pre-device metadata.
Determine whether root, overlayfs, remount, recovery, or manual partition writes changed source bytes.
fix_steps: Use an exact signed full OTA for the target build when the OEM supports it, because a full payload contains the complete final state rather than source-dependent deltas.
Otherwise restore the exact expected source state through an OEM-supported route before retrying the incremental update.
prerequisites: Exact source and target build identities, official full OTA, verified artifact digest, battery/power, and backup.
expected_outcomes: The update no longer depends on mismatched source partition bytes.
compatibility: A/B incremental/delta OTA failures with explicit source hash evidence.
known_incompatibility: A full OTA for another model, channel, or target build is not a substitute.
recovery_routes: Official full OTA or OEM software repair.

scope.scope_note: Platform A/B delta behavior; exact OEM source/target metadata remains mandatory.

records.title: A/B failed-update fallback depends on bootable and successful slot state
records.summary: A/B devices keep the current slot while writing the unused slot and should fall back when the new slot fails to boot. Blind slot switching can instead select incomplete data or collide with rollback protection.
symptoms: device bootloops after A/B OTA
device returns to previous build
one slot is marked unbootable
manual slot switch makes failure worse
diagnostic_steps: Read current-slot, active-slot, slot-successful, slot-unbootable, retry count, target build, and rollback evidence without changing them.
Determine whether the new slot ever reached the boot-successful milestone.
On Virtual A/B, also record snapshot merge status; dynamic partitions are snapshots rather than full physical duplicate slots.
fix_steps: Allow the bootloader's supported fallback when a valid previously successful slot exists.
Use an exact full OTA or OEM recovery when neither slot is a confirmed coherent boot set; do not toggle slots speculatively.
prerequisites: Read-only slot and snapshot evidence, exact builds for both slots, and rollback-state awareness.
expected_outcomes: A valid successful slot boots, or the absence of one is made explicit before recovery.
compatibility: Legacy A/B and Virtual A/B devices, with their different dynamic-partition representation.
known_incompatibility: Non-A/B devices have no equivalent slot fallback; an A/B slot label alone does not prove all partitions are duplicated.
recovery_routes: Exact full OTA, vendor rescue tool, or service when no coherent boot set remains.

scope.scope_note: Platform slot-state model; no slot mutation authority is granted.

records.title: AVB hash failure requires a consistent signed partition chain
records.summary: Verified Boot covers boot-critical and system/vendor partitions through signed hashes and chained metadata. Replacing only vbmeta or only boot may leave the chain inconsistent and cannot be generalized as an AVB fix.
symptoms: device refuses to boot after one partition was patched
dm-verity restarts device
corruption screen appears
AVB verification fails at boot
error_codes: No valid operating system could be found
diagnostic_steps: Record verified-boot state, lock state, root-of-trust fingerprint where exposed, rollback indices, and every descriptor/chain partition named by vbmeta.
Compare hashes and build provenance across boot, init_boot, vendor_boot, dtbo, vbmeta, system, vendor, product, and chained vbmeta partitions actually present.
Separate boot-time verification failure from runtime dm-verity EIO/restart behavior.
fix_steps: Restore a complete exact-build signed partition set through the OEM-supported recovery path or a separately verified rollback plan.
Preserve user data first when runtime eio mode still allows access; do not disable verification as a generic repair.
prerequisites: Exact target/build, AVB topology, trusted signed artifacts and hashes, lock state, rollback compatibility, backup, and rollback route.
expected_outcomes: Every verified descriptor resolves to matching signed partition content and the chain reaches an accepted root of trust.
compatibility: Android Verified Boot devices with observed hash, descriptor, or dm-verity evidence.
known_incompatibility: A generic blank vbmeta, verification-disable flag, or image from a nearby build can create new security and boot failures.
recovery_routes: OEM full image/OTA, official software repair, or exact signed-build reconstruction behind Guardian review.

scope.scope_note: Platform trust-chain guidance; exact descriptors determine which partitions belong to a device's chain.

records.title: Motorola capri maps several retail variants to one maintained device family
records.summary: LineageOS maintains moto g10, moto g10 power, and Lenovo K13 Note under capri, but explicitly notes that physical differences can remain. The alias helps discovery and never replaces exact model checks.
symptoms: Device DNA reports capri
retail name differs from ROM device page
Motorola and Lenovo names share a build family
diagnostic_steps: Read manufacturer, retail model, product, device codename, hardware SKU, region, and battery/product identifiers.
Match capri only when the maintained variant page includes the observed retail model.
Preserve retail-model differences even when one ROM build serves the family.
fix_steps: Use the capri-specific guide for the exact selected variant and stop if its model requirements do not match.
prerequisites: Exact retail model and hardware variant.
expected_outcomes: ROMVERSE can find capri documentation from any listed retail alias without claiming that the hardware is identical.
known_incompatibility: Other moto g, K-series, caprip, and similarly named models are not included.
recovery_routes: Select the exact variant on the maintainer page before using its guide.

scope.scope_note: Maintainer-published shared-build mapping; exact variant selection remains required.

records.title: Motorola caprip maps moto g30 and Lenovo K13 Pro
records.summary: The LineageOS caprip variant index maps moto g30 and Lenovo K13 Pro to one maintained build family while retaining their retail identities.
symptoms: Device DNA reports caprip
K13 Pro guide is listed with moto g30
retail name differs from codename
diagnostic_steps: Confirm product/device codename caprip and read the exact retail model and SKU.
Do not collapse caprip into capri; they are distinct maintained targets.
fix_steps: Use only the caprip guide after selecting the exact moto g30 or K13 Pro variant.
prerequisites: Exact model and caprip codename evidence.
expected_outcomes: Alias-aware lookup finds the correct caprip guide.
known_incompatibility: moto g10, moto g10 power, and K13 Note belong to capri, not caprip.
recovery_routes: Maintainer variant selector and exact device guide.

scope.scope_note: Maintainer-published alias map, explicitly distinct from capri.

records.summary: The maintainer variant index maps the 2015 Moto X Pure Edition and Moto X Style to clark, enabling alias-aware lookup without including later Moto X devices.

device marketed as Moto X Pure Edition
device marketed as Moto X Style
diagnostic_steps: Confirm codename clark, 2015 generation, and exact retail/SKU identity.
Exclude other Moto X generations even if the marketing name is similar.
fix_steps: Use clark-specific instructions only after the exact variant is selected.
prerequisites: Codename and generation evidence.
expected_outcomes: The two documented retail aliases resolve to the clark maintained target.
known_incompatibility: Other Moto X years and variants are outside this mapping.
recovery_routes: Maintainer variant page and exact clark guide.

records.title: Samsung klte model set requires exact Galaxy S5 LTE model and Android 6.0.1 firmware
records.summary: The maintained klte guide lists G900F/M/R4/R7/T/T3/V/W8 and requires the latest firmware from Android 6.0.1 even when installing a newer LineageOS branch.
symptoms: Device DNA reports klte
Galaxy S5 LTE firmware prerequisite warning
newer ROM expects older-numbered vendor firmware
diagnostic_steps: Read the complete SM-G900 model suffix rather than matching Galaxy S5 by name.
Record modem/bootloader firmware identity and compare it with the guide's Android 6.0.1 prerequisite.
Treat a ROM major-version downgrade as a fresh-install flow, not the ordinary updater path.
fix_steps: Follow the exact klte variant and firmware prerequisite from the maintained guide; use the latest security update within Android 6.0.1 when multiple releases exist.
prerequisites: Exact G900 variant, current firmware identity, maintained recovery, backup, and guide branch.
expected_outcomes: The ROM starts on its required vendor/bootloader firmware baseline.
known_incompatibility: Unlisted Galaxy S5 variants and similarly named devices are not included; Android 6.0.1 here is a firmware prerequisite, not the ROM platform version.
recovery_routes: Return to exact stock firmware or follow the klte fresh-install guide for downgrades.

scope.scope_note: Maintainer-published exact model set and firmware prerequisite for klte.

records.title: ASUS Z00T spans Zenfone 2 Laser and Zenfone 2 Selfie 1080p variants
records.summary: The LineageOS variant index maps two 1080p ASUS retail families to Z00T but notes physical differences, so screen resolution and exact model still matter.
symptoms: Device DNA reports Z00T
Zenfone retail name differs from maintained codename
Zenfone 2 Laser and Selfie share a build page
diagnostic_steps: Confirm Z00T, exact retail model, 1080p display variant, SKU, and camera/product differences.
Do not match lower-resolution or other Zenfone 2 variants by family name alone.
fix_steps: Choose the exact Z00T variant before using the maintained guide.
prerequisites: Exact ASUS model/SKU and display variant.
expected_outcomes: Alias lookup reaches Z00T without losing retail hardware distinctions.
known_incompatibility: Other Zenfone 2 resolutions, Z00L, and unrelated Zenfone models are excluded.
recovery_routes: Maintainer variant selector and exact ASUS stock recovery when unmatched.

scope.scope_note: Maintainer-published Z00T shared-build mapping limited to 1080p variants.

records.title: OnePlus 8T kebab regional model and build families must stay distinct
records.summary: The established XDA device guide maps KB2000 China, KB2001 India, KB2003 Europe, KB2005 international, and KB2007 T-Mobile variants. A boot image or firmware must match both model and build, not just kebab.
symptoms: Device DNA reports kebab
OnePlus 8T boot image lookup
regional KB model is required
diagnostic_steps: Read ro.product.model, ro.build.version.ota, ro.build.display.id, region/channel, DDR type where applicable, and current slot.
Map KB2000/1/3/5/7 as distinct regional variants under the OnePlus 8T family.
Reject a patched or stock boot image unless its exact build matches the live firmware.
fix_steps: Use only the exact variant/build guide and create patched images locally from the matching stock image when modification is intended.
prerequisites: Exact KB model, full build ID, image hash/provenance, slot evidence, backup, and rollback route.
expected_outcomes: Variant-aware lookup avoids cross-region boot-image and firmware mismatches.
known_incompatibility: A shared codename does not make regional firmware or boot images interchangeable.
recovery_routes: Exact regional stock package or OEM service route.

scope.scope_note: Established community-maintained variant map; exact build evidence remains mandatory.

records.title: Pixel 9 Pro caiman AP3A.241005.015 code 7 resolved after reset in one case
records.summary: One Pixel 9 Pro owner saw kInstallDeviceOpenError at about 47 percent across Windows, Linux, cables, and ports; a factory reset followed by the same Android 15 sideload reportedly succeeded.
symptoms: Pixel 9 Pro OTA sideload fails near 47 percent
multiple hosts and cables produce the same failure
Android 15 sideload aborts with status 1
diagnostic_steps: Require model/codename caiman, target AP3A.241005.015, current build, full recovery log, and exact OTA digest before using this case.
Confirm the failure is reproducible across a known-good cable/port and occurs after package verification.
Back up all accessible data and review less destructive official Pixel repair routes first.
fix_steps: The single report supports factory reset followed by retry only as a last-resort, explicitly data-erasing option for the same exact failure pattern.
Do not promise that reset repairs other ErrorCode 7 causes or preserves data.
prerequisites: Pixel 9 Pro/caiman identity, AP3A.241005.015 target, verified official OTA, known Google credentials, backup, and explicit acceptance of total userdata loss.
expected_outcomes: In the cited case, sideload proceeded after factory reset.
compatibility: Pixel 9 Pro caiman sideloading AP3A.241005.015 with the exact code 7/status 1 pattern.
known_incompatibility: One destructive success cannot be generalized to other Pixel models, builds, install targets, storage faults, or code-7 causes.
recovery_routes: Google Pixel Update and Software Repair or authorized Pixel service before destructive experimentation.

scope.scope_note: One explicit community success after a destructive reset; exact-model/build/error only and never automatic.

records.title: Moto G Pure XT2163-4 preflash validation blocks critical Android 11 downgrade images
records.summary: One unlocked XT2163-4 case reports lk, tee, sspm, and gz rejecting Android 11 with preflash validation while Motorola Rescue repeatedly restores the official Android 12 package.
symptoms: Moto G Pure bootloops after partial downgrade
critical MediaTek partitions reject flash
Motorola Rescue restores Android 12
diagnostic_steps: Confirm XT2163-4, original Android 12 state, unlocked status, and the exact partition/image versions attempted.
Treat missing fastboot variables or fastbootd access as capability evidence, not a path to bypass validation.
Use Motorola Rescue as the known recovery baseline and preserve its matched build identity.
fix_steps: Return to the current identity-matched official Android 12 image through Motorola Rescue when the downgrade leaves a bootloop.
Do not replace Rescue files after matching or force protected critical partitions.
prerequisites: Exact XT2163-4 identity, Windows/internet/USB for Rescue, Google credentials, backup where possible, and acceptance that Rescue erases user data.
expected_outcomes: The reported Rescue flow restores a booting official Android 12 state.
compatibility: Moto G Pure XT2163-4 originally shipped with Android 12 and matching this downgrade failure.
known_incompatibility: The report does not establish a safe Android 11 downgrade route; protected critical images remain rejected.
recovery_routes: Motorola Software Fix Rescue or Motorola service.

scope.scope_note: One detailed community case with repeated official Rescue recovery; no safe downgrade was demonstrated.

records.title: Moto Maxx XT1225 older GPT preflash rejection resolved with latest-package GPT in one case
records.summary: An XT1225 owner reports that an older GPT image produced preflash validation failure, while the GPT from the latest Marshmallow package was accepted and the remaining recovery completed.
symptoms: XT1225 fastboot recovery stops at GPT
older partition table image is rejected
device remains in bootloader
diagnostic_steps: Confirm XT1225, current bootloader/security version, region/channel, and exact attempted GPT provenance.
Treat GPT as critical partition-layout metadata; a wrong image can make all later partition offsets unsafe.
Locate only the exact newest official package for the device/channel and verify its digest before planning recovery.
fix_steps: The report supports using the exact latest compatible GPT rather than an older revision in a separately reviewed full-stock recovery plan.
Do not flash GPT from this anecdote without exact package verification and a service-grade rollback/recovery route.
prerequisites: Exact XT1225 variant and channel, verified full package and GPT hash, stable fastboot, battery, full backup where possible, and emergency recovery path.
expected_outcomes: In the cited case, GPT passed validation and the rest of the stock recovery restored boot.
compatibility: Moto Maxx XT1225 matching the cited bootloader generation and package channel.
known_incompatibility: No applicability to XT1254, other Motorola GPT layouts, or packages whose critical revisions are older than the device.
recovery_routes: Motorola Rescue if supported, exact full-stock service recovery, or authorized repair.

scope.scope_note: One owner-confirmed critical-image outcome; missing package hash keeps the record non-executable.

records.title: POCO F2 Pro lmi anti-rollback version 1 rejects package version 0
records.summary: In one lmi case, Fastboot reported device anti-rollback version 1 greater than package version 0. A stock V12.0.3.0.QJKMIXM MiFlash recovery restored MIUI, but the owner's clean-and-lock choice erased data and must not be copied automatically.
symptoms: POCO F2 Pro loops to recovery
Fastboot stock image is rejected by anti-rollback
custom ROM boot animation never finishes
error_codes: Current device antirollback version is greater than this package
diagnostic_steps: Confirm codename lmi, exact regional model, current anti value, package anti value, bootloader state, and installed/attempted MIUI builds.
Reject any package with a lower anti-rollback value and do not delete the script guard.
Separate stock-boot recovery from later custom-ROM compatibility; the thread restored MIUI before solving the ROM path.
fix_steps: Use only a verified exact-region stock package whose anti-rollback level is accepted by the device, through a separately reviewed Xiaomi recovery plan.
Never select bootloader relock unless the exact official region/build is confirmed and the user explicitly accepts data loss and brick risk.
prerequisites: Exact lmi model/region, current anti value, official package provenance/hash, unlocked state if required, stable Fastboot, backup, and rollback route.
expected_outcomes: The cited compatible stock build restored MIUI startup.
compatibility: POCO F2 Pro/Redmi K30 Pro lmi with device anti version 1 and exact V12.0.3.0.QJKMIXM stock context.
known_incompatibility: Package anti version 0 is rejected; clean-all-and-lock is destructive and can brick a mismatched region or modified device.
recovery_routes: Exact compatible Xiaomi stock recovery or authorized service/EDL when Fastboot is unavailable.

scope.scope_note: One explicit stock-restore outcome plus exact anti-version error; no relock or flash authority.

records.title: Galaxy M31s M317FXXU3DVH2 HASH_MISMATCH(3) requires coherent vbmeta recovery
records.summary: One M31s case reported ODIN MODE (AVB FAIL), custom VBMETA, and HASH_MISMATCH(3). A full power disconnect restored access to Download mode and a subsequent reflash reportedly recovered the device.
symptoms: Galaxy M31s is stuck in Odin AVB fail screen
normal key combinations do not leave error screen
custom vbmeta was installed
error_codes: vbmeta: Error verifying vbmeta image: HASH_MISMATCH(3)
diagnostic_steps: Confirm Galaxy M31s model, exact VBMETA build M317FXXU3DVH2, binary/CSC, and modification history.
Treat HASH_MISMATCH(3) as AVB chain evidence, not a USB transport error.
If the device cannot be powered down normally, use authorized service for a safe battery disconnect rather than instructing end-user disassembly.
fix_steps: Regain Download mode through the model's safe service procedure, then restore a complete exact-build signed stock set rather than an isolated guessed vbmeta.
Do not reuse a verification-disabled or custom vbmeta on a locked or stock recovery path.
prerequisites: Exact model/CSC/binary, trusted M317FXXU3DVH2-compatible stock package and hashes, stable Odin transport, safe power isolation, backup, and recovery route.
expected_outcomes: The cited owner regained Download mode and reported recovery after reflashing.
compatibility: Samsung Galaxy M31s with VBMETA M317FXXU3DVH2 and the exact HASH_MISMATCH(3) screen.
known_incompatibility: Physical disassembly is hazardous and not an end-user step; a vbmeta-only flash may leave other signed partitions inconsistent.
recovery_routes: Samsung authorized service for safe power isolation and exact stock restoration.

scope.scope_note: One exact-build community outcome; repair/service boundary replaces unsafe disassembly guidance.

records.title: sweetin package can falsely print mismatching image, but the guard must not be deleted
records.summary: One Redmi Note 10 Pro Max India owner found a sweetin script apparently rejecting a sweetin target and later succeeded using an older MiFlash release with an older stock build. The result is evidence of a tool/package defect, not permission to remove target guards.
symptoms: sweetin fastboot package rejects sweetin product
newer MiFlash and MIUI package fail
user intends to relock before resale
diagnostic_steps: Read fastboot product, retail model, Indian region code, bootloader state, package codename, script contents, package source/hash, and tool version.
Confirm the script is actually testing the observed product and that no wrapper changes the fastboot output format.
Do not delete or bypass the guard; obtain a known-good official package/tool combination or stop.
fix_steps: The report supports testing a vendor-compatible MiFlash version and a verified earlier same-region stock package when policy permits, without editing the product check.
Keep the bootloader unlocked until the exact official region/build has booted and relock compatibility is independently verified.
prerequisites: Redmi Note 10 Pro Max India, sweetin identity, exact regional package and hash, trusted tool version, backup, unlocked state, and rollback route.
expected_outcomes: In the cited case, older MiFlash plus an older same-device MIUI package completed without removing the identity guard.
compatibility: Redmi Note 10 Pro Max India sweetin matching the cited package-script behavior.
known_incompatibility: Deleting identity checks or relocking on a mismatched region can hard-brick; the exact working package digest was not preserved.
recovery_routes: Verified official sweetin fastboot package, Xiaomi service, or authorized EDL route if Fastboot recovery is unavailable.

scope.scope_note: One explicit community outcome for a suspected package/tool guard defect; no guard bypass or relock authority.
